page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-48GB is a cloud server instance belonging to the Cloud Native family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 shared vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The memory configuration provides 48.0 GB of RAM, translating to 3.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates a split performance profile. The instance registers poor single-core performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the bottom 10%, which is a typical tradeoff for shared CPU allocations. However, Geekbench single-core scores are strong, placing in the top 25%, and Geekbench text processing reaches the top tier. Multi-core performance across stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests consistently falls into the average category. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only and write operations on large blocks, also align with average tier performance.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the absence of local storage, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that require high core counts and moderate memory density without requiring dedicated CPU execution. It is suited for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, text processing, and static web serving, where resource sharing does not critically impact execution times. It is less suited for single-core intensive tasks or workloads requiring local NVMe storage.
